system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Each repair graph agent invoked by the dispatcher issues one LLM call using a specific prompt. The code and configuration agents share the same high-level prompt structure, but differ in their edit context
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt contains five ordered parts filled with per-case fault signature and candidates.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Each prompt contains five ordered parts: failure-side evidence from the fault signature, a structured edit context derived from localization, target-file context, a textual repair graph summary, and an exact-match edit instruction.
env_context_strategy.note: Localized candidates injected up front (closest to file_tree_summary) plus Exploration agent with file inspection/repository search (agent_driven_navigation).

context_compaction.evidence_quote: ORCA applies fixed caps per telemetry source across deployment substrates.
context_compaction.note: Caps on telemetry evidence entering the prompt; no history-level compaction described.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The fault signature is a structured textual summary of the differences between the failure telemetry and the reference telemetry.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The structured edit context is a JSON-formatted object that packages the localization output for the corresponding agent.
tool_call_format.note: Repair graph agents return an exact-match search-and-replace edit from one LLM call; the Exploration agent has an action space (read file, search, list dir, submit patch) but the call syntax is not stated.

tool_count.evidence_quote: an action space that includes file inspection, repository search, file editing, and validation commands
tool_count.note: Count of Exploration-agent action space; repair graph agents are single constrained LLM calls with no tools. ReAct baseline lists read file, search, list dir, submit patch.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The model must return an exact-match search-and-replace edit: the search text must be copied verbatim from the target file, and the replacement text specifies the new content for that region.
edit_primitive.note: Accepted edits are converted into a unified-diff patch candidate.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Each agent instance operates in a sandboxed repository workspace, with an action space that includes file inspection, repository search, file editing, and validation commands.
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: A deterministic dispatcher maps the localization outputs to the patch-generation agents in Algorithm 1.
loop_primitives.note: Default two-stage fixed pipeline; Exploration agent is an interactive loop; TGPV verification after generation; N independent Exploration runs with majority voting (default N=1).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: A deterministic dispatcher maps the localization outputs to the patch-generation agents in Algorithm 1.
planning_granularity.note: No plan object or planning step described; routing is rule-based.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: It uses a code repair graph agent for code candidates, a configuration repair graph agent for configuration candidates, and the Exploration agent when repair graph generation does not produce an accepted patch.
multi_agent_topology.note: Specialised agents dispatched deterministically; outputs merged.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: If no repair graph agent produces a candidate, Line 4 invokes the Exploration agent with the fault signature, ranked code candidates, and configuration candidates.
delegation_mechanism.note: Deterministic dispatcher hands the case to another specialised agent role.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: ORCA emits a unified-diff patch candidate for application code or deployment configuration.
human_in_loop.note: No human approval step described in the pipeline.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The structured edit context is a JSON-formatted object that packages the localization output for the corresponding agent.
short_term_state.note: Fault signature + candidate lists + repair graph carried through the pipeline.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: ORCA takes paired failure and reference telemetry bundles, the project workspace when available, and an optional issue title and body.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: An empty-edit check rejects outputs with no repository change and treats step-budget exhaustion without edits as an abstention.

self_verification.evidence_quote: TGPV therefore separates verification into four checks.
self_verification.note: C2 runs paired fault-revealing unit tests; C1/C2 check patch application and syntactic/semantic correctness (compilation); C4 replays telemetry. Verification is post-hoc, not fed back by default.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Unless otherwise stated, the main experiments use N=1 and an interaction-step budget of B=15 per instance.
retry_policy.note: Configurable fixed_n via N independent Exploration-agent runs (N in {1,3,5}) combined by majority voting; default N=1.

rollback.evidence_quote: Each agent instance operates in a sandboxed repository workspace, with an action space that includes file inspection, repository search, file editing, and validation commands.
rollback.note: No undo/revert mechanism described; rejected edits are simply not converted to a patch.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: An instance either produces repository edits that are converted into a unified-diff patch candidate or abstains when it cannot identify a repair location.
termination_condition.note: Step-budget B=15 per Exploration instance; repair graph agents are single calls.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Efficiency is reported as average token cost and wall-clock time per case.
cost_controls.note: Token cost is measured, not capped; no caching or routing mechanism described (the deterministic dispatcher routes agents, not models).

timeouts.evidence_quote: Unless otherwise stated, the main experiments use N=1 and an interaction-step budget of B=15 per instance.
timeouts.note: Only a step budget, which is not a timeout; wall-clock time is reported but not enforced.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: we identify the versions immediately before and after the repair and deploy both in containerized environments
execution_isolation.note: Exploration agent operates in a sandboxed repository workspace; TGPV redeploys the patched stack.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Each agent instance operates in a sandboxed repository workspace
filesystem_access.note: Repair graph agents are further scoped: the context defines the target locations the model may edit.

permission_model.evidence_quote: In both repair graph agents, the context defines the target locations the model may edit and the telemetry evidence associated with those locations.
permission_model.note: Edit locations restricted to localized candidates; exact-match check rejects other edits.

tracing.evidence_quote: ORCA checks each generated patch along four axes: patch validity, syntactic and semantic correctness, test-oracle integrity, and telemetry replay.
tracing.note: Per-case verifier outcomes are returned with the patch; no explicit trace-logging facility described for this ORCA.

replayability.evidence_quote: This check redeploys the patched stack, replays the same traffic profile, and recomputes the telemetry signal associated with the failure-side fault signature.
replayability.note: Telemetry replay of workload, not of agent trajectories; T=0 used to keep generation deterministic.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: The resulting patch candidate is evaluated by the Telemetry-Grounded Patch Verifier (TGPV), which reports patch validity, syntactic and semantic correctness, test-oracle integrity, and telemetry replay.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation runner and 575-case benchmark ship with the system; benchmark to be made publicly available.

guardrails.evidence_quote: The agent accepts the output only when the search text matches the target file exactly; otherwise it rejects the edit before verifier execution.
guardrails.note: Input sanitization: ORCA sanitizes the issue title and body to reduce solution leakage; TGPV C3 flags patches that edit test files.

target_domain.evidence_quote: We present ORCA, an observability-grounded APR pipeline for microservice incidents.

open_source.note: Benchmark stated to be made publicly available; no licence or code release statement for the system.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We compare seven LLMs from four providers: DeepSeek-V4-pro, DeepSeek-Flash, Claude-Opus-4.8, GPT-5.1, GPT-5-mini, GPT-4o-mini, and Qwen3-Coder-30B

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: We propose ORCA, an observability-grounded automated program repair pipeline for microservice incidents.
primary_artifact.note: No repository URL given in the evidence.
